line: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 O-O f3
teaches: The modest f-pawn move is the spine of this whole setup: it bolts the centre shut so that everything that follows — the bishop's development, the queen behind it, castling long, the pawn storm — happens behind a wall. Judge it by what it enables, not by what it looks like.
explains: The pawn on f3 defends the pawn on e4, and with the centre held by pawns alone the pieces are free to take up attacking posts instead of guard duty. The fianchettoed bishop across the board now stares into a wall that never needs a defender.

line: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 O-O f3 d6 Be3 e5 d5 c6 Qd2 Bd7 O-O-O b5 dxc6 Nxc6 Nxb5
teaches: Whether you can accept a pawn offer depends on your structure, not your nerve. A setup with no weaknesses behind it can open the centre and grab material without exposing anything — count your loose pieces and pawn holes first, and when the count says none, take.
explains: The knight has taken the pawn on b5 and immediately attacks two more — the pawn on d6 and the pawn on a7. Nothing in the position hangs back home: the centre is bolted, development is finished, and the pawn grab is just good bookkeeping.
